evaluations.title: Double-Centered Prompt-by-Token Matrix vs Shuffled Text
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a prompt-by-token logit matrix using natural text vs. token-shuffled text. Applies row and column mean-centering to isolate context-token interaction from base frequencies. Compares singular value spectra and rank-r reconstruction error to evaluate whether natural text shows non-trivial low-rank structure.

evaluations.title: Exploratory Context-Probe Transfer Landscape
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory landscape experiment constructing three candidate logit tables, with the composed context-probe transfer table treated as the primary hypothesized nontrivial table. The goal is to compare low-rank metrics, held-out reconstruction, centering ablations, and controls before any later precommitted validation.

evaluations.title: Subspace Transfer of Composed Context-Probe Delta Matrices
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the low-rank subspace derived from natural context-probe interactions is structurally more meaningful than the subspace from shuffled contexts. Constructs composed delta matrices for natural, shuffled, and held-out contexts. Compares how well the singular vectors of the natural vs. shuffled matrices reconstruct the held-out natural matrix.

evaluations.title: Doubly Mean-Centered Context-by-Active-Token Matrix vs Token-Shuffled Control
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs an N x V_active logit table (contexts by active tokens) using double mean-centering to isolate context-token interactions. Evaluates whether natural text contexts yield a lower effective rank than token-shuffled contexts.

evaluations.title: Context-Probe Interaction Rank via Double-Centering
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the low-rank structure of the interaction between contexts and probes. To isolate the true compositional effect from unigram and baseline biases, we double-center the logit matrix (removing row and column means) before SVD. We compare the singular value decay and reconstruction KL of the natural context-probe matrix against a control matrix that uses corrupted probes, keeping the selected token axis identical.

evaluations.title: Null-calibrated spectra of logit tables: descriptive ground truth
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Establish the empirical singular-value spectra of two logit-table constructions (context-by-token, and composed context x intervention) for OLMo-1B, and calibrate apparent low-rank structure against a ladder of structure-preserving null models. This is a descriptive run aimed at the positive question: do any singular values robustly exceed a structure-preserving null edge, and how does the spike count change as each null destroys one more kind of structure?

evaluations.title: Landscape of low-rank structure in OLMo-1B composed logit tables (Exp1)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory pipeline+landscape run. Build three candidate logit tables (local baseline, absolute composed, intervention-effect delta) on shared fragments, measure their low-rank spectra under four centering schemes, and compare against matched-marginal null controls. Goal: establish timing, corpus, and which table shows excess low-rank concentration beyond matched nulls, to inform a later pre-registered held-out claim. This is NOT a headline scientific claim.

evaluations.title: Context-Probe Control Taxonomy
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Focused follow-up to Eval #2. The prior T3 context-probe transfer table showed strong covariance relative to marginal controls but did not separate from corrupted contexts. This experiment decomposes the control: natural contexts are compared with within-context word shuffles, global-pool word shuffles, and length-matched unigram-resampled contexts to test whether T3 low-rank structure depends on word order, lexical inventory, or generic word-distribution effects.

evaluations.title: Ablation on Centering Order in Subspace Transfer
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the mathematical order of centering and baseline subtraction in the composed context-probe delta matrix. Compares Global Flattened Centering (Eval 3) against Local Block Centering to determine if the positive subspace transfer results are robust to the exact definition of logit interaction.

evaluations.title: Low-Rank Compositionality: Precontext-by-Probe Interaction Matrix
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a block matrix where rows are natural pre-contexts and column blocks represent the model's response to different appended probes. Evaluates whether natural probe interactions exhibit a lower effective rank than token-shuffled probe interactions.

evaluations.title: Pre-registered held-out validation of low-rank structure in OLMo-1B effect table (Exp2)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Pre-registered confirmatory test of whether the double-centered intervention-effect (delta) composed logit table TB exhibits low-rank structure that generalizes out-of-sample. Uses a 2x2 context/probe bi-cross-validation split to measure held-out-context (Q21) and strict held-out-both (Q22) rank-8 reconstruction error against within-column-permutation and probe-block-shuffle matched-marginal nulls, across >=3 seeds, plus a token-shuffled-text comparison. Headline metric pre-registered: Q22 rank-8 relative Frobenius gap vs within-column null.

evaluations.title: Structural vs. Random Token Probes Interaction Matrix
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether concatenating specific structural/grammatical words to a context induces a lower-rank interaction space than concatenating arbitrary/random words. We manually define a set of structural probes and a set of random probes, build the respective context-probe matrices, double-center them, and compare their singular value decay. This addresses the limitation of Eval 5, where randomly concatenated wiki fragments created unnatural context switches.

evaluations.title: Precommitted Validation of Composed Order-Residual T3
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Precommitted validation of the composed order-residual table identified in Eval #8. The primary table is T3_natural minus an independently within-context-shuffled T3, with fresh seeds and strict controls including shuffle-shuffle deltas and column-marginal permutations. The primary metric is rank-8 held-out row reconstruction gain over rank-0.

evaluations.title: Compositional Delta Matrix: Pre-context Update to Probe Logits
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the rank of the pure compositional interaction between pre-contexts and probes. Constructs a doubly mean-centered matrix of logit updates: Delta = L(Context+Probe) - L(Probe). Hypothesizes that natural probes yield lower-rank updates than within-probe shuffled probes.

evaluations.title: Where does the held-out low-rank interaction live? Corruption ladder for OLMo-1B effect table (Exp3)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Characterizes the reproducible held-out low-rank structure of the double-centered intervention-effect table TB (confirmed in Eval #11). Eval #11 showed the held-out gap is invariant to probe word-shuffling. This experiment runs a corruption ladder (natural / probe-word-shuffle / probe-random-token / context-word-shuffle / context-random-token) under the identical bi-cross-validation Q22 protocol to localize whether the structure depends on probe content, context content, or neither, and maps the held-out gap as a function of rank r to estimate the effective transferable rank with seed confidence intervals.

evaluations.title: Order-Delta Fresh-Seed Power Extension
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Fresh-seed power extension of the failed Eval #13 validation. The table, token rule, transform, and primary metric remain fixed: column-centered T3_order_delta rank-8 held-out row reconstruction gain. The goal is not to move thresholds but to test whether the same effect clears the original threshold on a larger fresh seed set; otherwise the T3_order_delta thread should be deprioritized.

evaluations.title: Intervention Delta Matrix: Positional Token Deletion vs Random Deletion
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a context-by-intervention matrix where columns represent specific token deletions. Evaluates if the predictive vulnerability profile (logit deltas) has a lower rank for structured positional deletions (e.g., last N tokens) compared to random token deletions.

evaluations.title: Multi-Probe Interaction Subspace via Independent Permutation
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the logit shifts induced by different probes on a shared context lie in a low-dimensional subspace. We build a double-centered Context x Probe matrix and compare its singular value decay against a rigorous control: independent column permutation. This control breaks the inter-probe correlation for each context while preserving the exact marginal distributions. A significantly faster decay in the true matrix proves that different probes activate a shared, low-rank representation of the context.

evaluations.title: Scalar Context-Probe Compatibility Residuals
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory fallback after the T3_order_delta validation and power extension failed against shuffle-shuffle controls. This experiment constructs scalar context-probe matrices using true continuation targets from probe fragments, additive residuals, contrastive target-vs-distractor shifts, target-permutation controls, and masked-entry or held-out reconstruction metrics.

evaluations.title: Composition reveals contextual low-rank structure: alignment-null calibration
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Regular-paper experiment. Building on descriptive ground truth (Eval #6), I test whether the composed context x intervention logit table contains low-rank structure that specifically reflects the SAME context responding coherently across DIFFERENT interventions, beyond column marginals, token selection, and global mean shifts, and whether that structure generalizes to held-out contexts. The crux control is a novel per-block row-alignment permutation null derived from a context-Gram decomposition (G = sum_j M_j M_j^T): coherent cross-block subspace sharing makes top Gram eigenvalues add across blocks, which the alignment null collapses. Primary metric is the held-out captured-energy curve versus chance (s/n), a column-permutation null, and

evaluations.title: Subspace Transfer with Syntactic Token Selection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the token selection rule in the Composed Delta Subspace Transfer test. Instead of selecting the top-k tokens predicted by each probe, this evaluation restricts the column dimension entirely to a fixed set of common English syntactic function words. This tests the hypothesis that the non-trivial low-rank interaction structure is heavily concentrated in syntactic expectations.

evaluations.title: What does the content-robust low-rank context code encode? Surface-feature decomposition (Exp4)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: The held-out low-rank interaction structure of the double-centered intervention-effect table TB (Eval #11, #15) is content-robust: it survives random-token corruption. This experiment tests WHAT that transferable structure encodes by regressing the bi-cross-validation context codes on simple surface/positional features (context token length, last-token id/log-frequency, mean logit norm, next-token entropy) fitted on training contexts only, and measuring (a) how much context-code variance these features explain on held-out contexts, and (b) whether the held-out Q22 reconstruction gap survives after projecting out the surface-feature-predictable component. Distinguishes surface-driven from residual structure.

evaluations.title: Scaled Intervention Delta Matrix: Expanded Contexts and Deletion Window
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the positional token-deletion logit-delta experiment (Eval #17) to a larger matrix size. Expands contexts (N=128) and doubles the positional intervention window (M=20) to test if the low-rank vulnerability profile persists beyond the immediate 10-token trailing window.

evaluations.title: Subspace Transfer with Semantic Token Selection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the token selection rule in the Composed Delta Subspace Transfer test by restricting the column dimension entirely to a fixed set of common semantic content words (nouns). This serves as the comparative counterpart to Eval 21 (Syntactic Tokens) to test whether semantic interactions are less structurally distinct from bag-of-words (shuffled) predictions.

evaluations.title: Is the residual low-rank structure linguistic? Corruption x surface decomposition (Exp5)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #22 showed ~2/3 of the held-out low-rank gap in the double-centered intervention-effect table TB is explained by six simple context surface/logit features, leaving a residual gap of ~0.09. This experiment tests whether that residual is linguistic by crossing the corruption ladder (natural vs context-random-token) with the surface-feature decomposition: it measures full / surface-only / residual Q22 held-out gaps under each corruption condition. If the residual gap collapses under context-random-token while the surface-only gap persists, the residual reflects linguistic content; if the residual survives random tokens, even the residual is non-linguistic.

evaluations.title: Token-Axis Invariance in Multi-Probe Subspace (Random Tokens)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: An ablation on Eval 18 to test token-axis invariance. We reconstruct the Context x Probe matrix using exactly the same setup as Eval 18, but instead of selecting the top-50 tokens for each probe, we select a fixed set of 50 random tokens from the vocabulary across all probes. We compare the double-centered true matrix to the independent block-permuted control to verify if the alignment gap persists when the token axis is decoupled from the probes.

evaluations.title: Ablating Target Token Rule: Top-K Active Tokens in Deletion Delta Matrix
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the target-token selection rule in the structured deletion-delta experiment (Evals #17, #23). Replaces the single argmax target with a block of the top-K active tokens for each context to test if the low-rank vulnerability profile is a general property of the active decision space.

evaluations.title: Feature-Conditioned Alignment Null for TB Context Codes
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the held-out alignment gap in the double-centered TB effect table survives a stronger null that preserves coarse surface-feature alignment across intervention blocks. This complements prior linear surface-feature residualization by using nonparametric feature-stratified row-alignment permutations as controls.

evaluations.title: Linguistic vs distributional: frequency-matched context control for TB low-rank structure (Exp6)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #25 showed the held-out low-rank gap of the double-centered intervention-effect table TB survives uniform-random context tokens (content-robust), but the surface-feature decomposition collapsed because uniform random tokens are out-of-distribution. This experiment adds a frequency-matched random context control (context tokens sampled from the corpus unigram distribution, preserving token-frequency statistics and length while destroying linguistic content and order) to separate linguistic dependence from mere distributional shift. It compares full / surface-only / residual held-out Q22 gaps and feature-to-code R2 across natural, uniform-random, and frequency-matched-random contexts.

evaluations.title: Context Content Ablation in Multi-Probe Subspace (Shuffled Contexts)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: An ablation on Eval 18 to test context content dependence. We reconstruct the double-centered Context x Probe interaction matrix and its independent block-permuted control, but we first apply token-level shuffling to the context strings. This preserves length and surface statistics while destroying linguistic coherence. We test whether the low-rank alignment gap between the true and permuted matrices persists, shrinks, or disappears when contexts lack semantic meaning.

evaluations.title: Subspace Transfer Scalability and Sample Efficiency
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the robustness of the Subspace Transfer Test across varying numbers of training contexts. By sweeping the number of training contexts across [32, 64, 128] while keeping the held-out validation set fixed, this experiment tests whether the predictive quality of the natural interaction subspace improves with more data and whether the margin over the corrupted (shuffled) subspace remains stable.

evaluations.title: Ablating Intervention Mechanism: Positional Token Masking vs Deletion
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the intervention mechanism of the deletion-delta matrix (Eval #23). Replaces the 'delete' operation with a 'mask' or 'blank' operation (replacing the target token with a neutral token). Tests if the low-rank vulnerability profile is driven by semantic/syntactic information loss rather than mere positional embedding shifts caused by sequence length changes.

evaluations.title: Replicating Feature-Conditioned Alignment Nulls
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Replication and strengthening of Eval #28. Tests whether the empirical held-out captured-energy gap over a surface-cluster feature-conditioned alignment null remains positive for a double-centered delta-TB table with more fresh seeds and more null replicates, while adding single-centering and raw-composed variants as secondary centering/table-definition checks.

evaluations.title: A coherence law for composed logit tables: cross-intervention subspace transfer and B-scaling
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Regular-paper experiment going beyond null-gap detection to a generative account of WHY composed context x intervention tables are low-rank. Using a context-Gram decomposition G = sum_j M_j M_j^T, I test whether different interventions activate a COMMON context subspace by estimating that subspace from disjoint FIT interventions and measuring captured energy of HELD-OUT interventions against chance (r/m) and an incoherent row-alignment null. I then characterize how the top context-Gram eigenvalue grows with the number of interventions B, and distinguish a fixed-shared-subspace-plus-incoherent-noise law from a growing-shared-dimension law, with a per-block whitening control to rule out heteroscedasticity.

evaluations.title: Cross-Probe Manifold Transfer: Held-Out Predictive Subspace
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the shared context subspace discovered in Eval 18 generalizes to held-out probes. We split 32 probes into 16 train and 16 test probes. We learn the context basis (left singular vectors) by applying SVD to the double-centered train matrix. We then project the double-centered test matrix onto this basis and measure the reconstruction error. We compare this to the reconstruction error of a control test matrix where contexts are independently permuted within each block. A lower error on the true test matrix proves out-of-sample subspace transfer.

evaluations.title: Is the natural subspace linguistically special or just distribution-matched? Crossover subspace transfer (Exp7)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #1 (Lumina) reports that a natural-text interaction subspace reconstructs held-out natural language better than a word-shuffled subspace, concluding the structure is fully compositional. We test an alternative explanation: the natural-over-shuffled margin reflects train/target DISTRIBUTION MATCH rather than linguistic specialness. We run a crossover subspace-transfer matrix on the double-centered intervention-effect table TB: fit rank-r right-singular subspaces on training contexts from {natural, frequency-matched-random, word-shuffled} and evaluate reconstruction on held-out targets from {natural, frequency-matched-random}. Diagonal (matched-distribution) dominance would indicate a distribution-match effect; natural-row dominance would support linguistic specialness.

evaluations.title: Locating the Dimensionality Elbow of the Interaction Subspace
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the precise dimensionality of the compositional interaction subspace by evaluating held-out subspace transfer error at high rank granularity. By sweeping the evaluated rank from $r=1$ up to $r=64$, we aim to locate the 'elbow' where adding dimensions ceases to improve transfer over the shuffled-context baseline, separating true structural factors from idiosyncratic noise.

evaluations.title: Compositional Vulnerability: Syntactic vs Semantic Target Logit Deltas
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the low-rank positional vulnerability profile is specific to syntactic routing or general to semantic content. Expands the dynamic mask-delta framework (Eval #32) to track logit deltas for fixed lists of 25 function words and 25 common nouns, forming 128 x 500 block matrices. Tests if both spaces are low-rank compared to random mask controls, and contrasts their relative dimensionality.

evaluations.title: Context-Alone Predictive-State Conditioned Alignment Null
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic follow-up to the replicated feature-conditioned alignment-null result. It tests whether the residual double-centered delta-TB alignment gap left after simple surface/logit feature conditioning can be explained by a richer black-box context-alone predictive-state sketch: low-dimensional features derived from context-alone next-token logits.

evaluations.title: Linguistic vs Distributional: Shuffled Context Ablation of the Vulnerability Profile
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Directly tests whether the low-rank vulnerability profile is genuinely linguistic or merely a distributional artifact (as proposed in Archive #4). Compares the effective rank of positional mask-delta matrices derived from natural contexts against those derived from within-context token-shuffled contexts, using fixed sets of syntactic and semantic target tokens.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Subspace Factorization: Isolating Meaning from Anomaly
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the geometric overlap between the interaction subspace of natural text and the interaction subspace of token-shuffled text. We derive context bases (left singular vectors) independently from a Natural Context x Probe matrix and a Shuffled Context x Probe matrix. We then project the natural matrix onto the shuffled basis to quantify the variance explained purely by surface/anomaly factors. Crucially, we analyze the orthogonal complement (the residual) to determine if a uniquely linguistic, non-surface subspace exists that retains cross-probe low-rank alignment.

evaluations.title: Optimized Replication of Context-Alone Conditioned Null
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Optimized replication of Eval #39 at the Eval #33 scale. Tests whether conditioning the row-alignment null on both simple surface features and context-alone logit PCs still leaves a stable residual held-out captured-energy gap in the double-centered delta-TB table, while avoiding the auxiliary nulls that caused Eval #39 to downscale.

evaluations.title: Effective dimension and coherence scaling of the composed-table shared subspace
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Regular-paper experiment establishing a generative, quantitative account of the shared context subspace in the double-centered composed context x intervention table for OLMo-1B. Going beyond gap detection (Archive #3) and the surface/linguistic decomposition (Archive #4), I (1) disentangle subspace-estimation quality from structure by measuring the asymptotic cross-intervention transfer fraction as the number of fit interventions grows, (2) estimate the effective dimension d* of the shared subspace via two independent estimators (out-of-sample transfer knee vs context-Gram eigenvalues above an incoherent null) and test their agreement, and (3) characterize the coherence scaling law of the top context-Gram eigenvalue with the number of interventions

evaluations.title: Subspace Transfer: Distributional vs Compositional (Syntactic Token Focus)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the interaction subspace of syntactic function words is driven by true linguistic compositionality (word order) or merely distributional surface features. Constructs four training subspaces (Natural, Within-Prompt Shuffle, Frequency-Matched Random, and Uniform Random) using Method B and restricted to 25 syntactic tokens. Evaluates the relative Frobenius reconstruction error of a fixed Held-out Natural Matrix on all four subspaces to test whether frequency-matching fails to capture syntactic routing.

evaluations.title: Does a subject-verb agreement logit table escape the distributional manifold? Order-sensitivity differential (Exp8)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #4 showed the held-out low-rank structure of the wiki intervention-effect table TB is content-robust: it survives unigram-frequency-matched scrambling, hence is surface/distributional rather than linguistic. This experiment tests whether a construction governed by a long-range syntactic dependency escapes that distributional manifold. We build a subject-verb number-agreement profile table (rows = contexts varying subject/distractor number and position; columns = signed inflection-contrast logits log P(correct verb form) - log P(incorrect) for a battery of verb lemmas) and measure, via leakage-controlled bi-cross-validation against a within-column row-permutation null, the ORDER-SENSITIVITY DIFFERENTIAL: how much word-order shuffling and frequency-matched scrambling collapse the held-out gap for

evaluations.title: Isolating Structural Alignment: Independent Permutation Control on the Vulnerability Profile
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the 'informational collapse' artifact where models respond to corrupted text with low-dimensional priors (Eval #40). Applies an Independent Column Permutation Control to the Positional Mask Delta Matrix. This preserves the exact marginal distribution of logit updates for every mask/target combination while destroying within-context correlations, providing an artifact-free test of nontrivial low-rank structural alignment.

evaluations.title: Top-Direction Decomposition of Delta-TB Context Codes
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Mechanism follow-up to Evals #33 and #42. Instead of only challenging the low-rank subspace with feature-conditioned nulls, this experiment decomposes individual delta-TB context-code directions: how much of each top held-out-transfer direction is predicted by simple surface features and context-alone logit PCs, and how much captured energy remains in residual codes.

evaluations.title: Order-dependence of the agreement subspace via distribution-matched crossover (Exp9)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #45 showed that for a subject-verb agreement logit table, the held-out rank-r gap vs a permutation null does NOT collapse under scrambling - it increases - because corruption simplifies the logit manifold, confounding gap-vs-null as a detector of linguistic structure. This experiment uses a distribution-match-controlled crossover that sidesteps that confound: it fits the rank-r subspace on natural, word-shuffled, or frequency-matched agreement training contexts and evaluates reconstruction on the SAME natural held-out agreement target. If the agreement structure is order-dependent (linguistic), the scrambled-trained subspace reconstructs the natural target worse than the natural-trained subspace; the train-source penalty should be much larger

evaluations.title: Ablating Context-Logit PC Sources for Delta-TB Context-Code Prediction
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests why context-alone logit PCs predict double-centered delta-TB context codes so well. It keeps the Eval #47 context-code setup fixed, then varies the source token set and number of PCs used as predictors, with the primary precommitted contrast asking whether prediction remains strong when context-alone PCs are computed from tokens disjoint from the delta-TB probe-token columns.

evaluations.title: Statistical Rigor of Structural Alignment: Multi-Draw Permutation Control
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Strengthens the findings of Eval #46 by executing a multi-draw independent column permutation control. Ensures the massive rank gap between the Natural Mask-Delta Matrix and the Permuted Matrix is robust to the variance of the permutation sampling distribution.

evaluations.title: Distribution-matched crossover maps the order-dependence boundary: agreement & function-word vs wiki tables (Exp10)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidating experiment. Eval #45 showed gap-vs-permutation-null is a confounded detector of order-dependent linguistic structure because corruption simplifies the logit manifold; Eval #48 and Lumina's Eval #44 showed a distribution-matched crossover (all trained subspaces evaluated on the same natural held-out target) reveals order-dependent structure in agreement and function-word tables. This experiment cleanly compares three constructions under the identical crossover: (1) a subject-verb agreement contrast table with a restored strong agreement signal and expanded lexical diversity, (2) a syntactic function-word contrast table (own implementation), and (3) the Archive #4 wiki TB intervention-effect table as reference.
