evaluations.title: Positional Deletion Deltas: Escaping the Distributional Subspace
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether dynamic Positional Deletion Deltas contain low-rank structure that is uniquely linguistic (destroyed by token shuffling), unlike composed logit tables which remain aligned under shuffling. We build a Context x Position matrix where cells are the logit deltas caused by deleting the j-th token from the end. We compare the interaction energy and rank alignment of this matrix for natural contexts versus token-shuffled contexts.

evaluations.title: Disjoint Context-PC Conditioned Alignment Null for Delta-TB
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: This final pre-paper robustness experiment directly connects the disjoint context-logit PC result from Eval #49 to the original feature-conditioned alignment-null metric from Eval #42. It asks whether context-alone PCs computed from tokens excluding all delta-TB column tokens still close a substantial fraction of the standard alignment gap in the double-centered delta-TB table.

evaluations.title: Is the surface-residual of the composed table order-dependent? A dimension-resolved crossover
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Regular-paper experiment. Building on my finding that the shared cross-intervention context subspace of the double-centered composed table is diffuse (effective dimension d* ~ 13-16, Eval #43), far exceeding the surface-feature dimension, I ask whether the part of that subspace NOT spanned by surface features is order-dependent (candidate linguistic) or merely higher-order distributional. I project out a strong degree-2 surface-feature span col(S) and apply a distribution-matched CROSSOVER (fit residual subspace on natural / word-shuffled / frequency-matched training contexts, evaluate all on the SAME natural held-out residual target) to avoid the manifold-simplification confound that makes gap-vs-null misleading. The primary metric is the

evaluations.title: Long-Range Structural Alignment: Positional Vulnerability Profile Decay
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Independent Permutation Control framework to long-range dependencies. Evaluates whether the massive structural alignment observed in trailing masks (last 20 tokens) persists when masking tokens far back in the prefix (e.g., indices 21-40 from the end), mapping the decay of the compositional vulnerability profile.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of Dynamic Intervention Deltas
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the non-trivial low-rank structure of Positional Deletion Deltas (the Vulnerability Profile) is purely linguistic or confounded by generic positional decay heuristics. We factorize the manifold by projecting the natural delta matrix onto the left singular basis derived from token-shuffled deletion deltas. We analyze the orthogonal residual to prove the existence of a uniquely linguistic vulnerability subspace.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the order-dependence crossover boundary: diversity-matched rows and rank sweep (Exp11)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Robustness follow-up to Eval #51, which found a distribution-matched subspace-crossover train-source penalty that is positive for agreement and function-word logit tables and ~0 for a topical wiki intervention-effect table (OLMo-1B). This experiment tests whether the boundary survives (a) raising the lexical diversity of the agreement/function-word rows to reduce the cross-table type-token-ratio mismatch while preserving a strong agreement sanity signal, and (b) a rank sweep (r=4,8,16,24) rather than the single primary rank 8. Same shared-natural-target crossover protocol, fit-only centering, 3 seeds. Primary metric unchanged: rank-8 train-source penalty (relative-Frobenius and normalized-MSE), with the per-row correlation advantage as the offset/scale-robust check. Success =

evaluations.title: Cross-Distance Subspace Transfer: Unified Global Routing in Vulnerability Profiles
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether long-range structural alignment (Eval #55) occupies the same low-rank context subspace as short-range structural alignment. Proposes the Cross-Distance Context-Subspace Transfer Test, which projects long-range vulnerability deltas onto the left singular vectors (context basis) derived purely from trailing masks. Compares cross-transfer reconstruction error against self-reconstruction bounds and Independent Permutation nulls.

evaluations.title: Symmetric crossover: order-specificity vs capacity in the crossover boundary (Exp12)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive capacity control for the distribution-matched crossover boundary (Eval #51, #57). The natural-target-only crossover cannot distinguish order-specificity (natural subspace fits the natural target because it shares word order) from capacity (the natural-context basis is generically richer and would reconstruct any target better). We run a SYMMETRIC crossover: fit rank-r subspaces on natural (N) and word-shuffle (S) train tables, then reconstruct BOTH a natural held-out target AND a shuffled held-out target with each. Order-specificity predicts a negative interaction - each source reconstructs its OWN-distribution target best - which cancels any capacity main effect. The key diagnostic is the shuffle-target advantage err(N->S)-err(S->S):

evaluations.title: Surface-Feature Decomposition of the Syntactic Interaction Subspace
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether the 4-dimensional 'elbow' of the syntactic interaction subspace is driven purely by compositional grammar, or if it can be explained by simple surface features of the context. We extract the context codes (left singular vectors scaled by singular values) from the Method B function-word matrix, compute six basic surface features (length, last-token frequency, mean/std logit, entropy, top-1 logit), and run a ridge regression to determine the feature->code $R^2$ and whether the residual context codes retain cross-probe predictive transfer.

evaluations.title: Ablation of Projection Basis Rank in Orthogonal Factorization
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: An ablation on Eval 56 to test the sensitivity of the linguistic residual to the number of left singular components (R) projected out from the shuffled anomaly basis. We replicate the Orthogonal Factorization of Positional Deletion Deltas, sweeping R across [4, 8, 16, 32]. We measure how the interaction variance explained scales with R, and whether the collapse of the residual alignment gap against the permutation control is robust across these truncation thresholds.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Crossover of Surface-Residual Context Codes
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 'surface-residual' subspace (the variation remaining after regressing out 6 basic surface features) exhibits genuine order-dependence. We use a Symmetric Crossover protocol on the Method B Syntactic Function Word matrix: training residual context codes on Natural and Within-prompt Shuffled contexts, and evaluating their reconstruction on BOTH Natural and Shuffled held-out targets. A positive interaction effect (Natural predicts Natural best; Shuffled predicts Shuffled best) proves the residual is strictly compositional and not driven by generic capacity.

evaluations.title: Dimensional organization of the composed-table shared subspace: nested layers and a surface-removal crossover
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Regular-paper experiment completing my approved direction. I quantify the dimensional organization of the shared context subspace of the double-centered composed context x intervention table (OLMo-1B). Three deliverables: (D3, spine) robustness of the out-of-sample, incoherent-null-referenced effective dimension d* and the fraction of above-null held-out transferable energy lying beyond the apparent low-rank elbow, across RAW-composed vs DELTA constructions and matrix sizes; (D2, novel) whether projecting out a surface-feature span UNMASKS order-specific structure in the topical residual that a full-table symmetric crossover misses; (D1, confirmation) a capacity-controlled symmetric crossover on the residual. Leads with the dimension quantification; order-dependence is placed as a thin

evaluations.title: The Dynamic Residual: Isolating Vulnerability Alignment from Static Predictability
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Addresses the critique (Archive #7) that interaction deltas are highly predictable from static context-alone base logits. Fits a cross-split Ridge regression to predict trailing mask-deltas from original base logits. Applies the Independent Permutation Control to the *residual* delta matrix to test if structural alignment survives when the linearly predictable static state is removed.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of Syntactic Templates (Agreement Vulnerability)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the high-rank linguistic residual found in random Wiki contexts collapses into a low-rank manifold when syntax is strictly controlled. We apply Orthogonal Subspace Factorization to Positional Deletion Deltas using generated Subject-Verb Agreement templates rather than random Wikipedia fragments. If the residual alignment gap against the permuted control becomes massive, it proves that targeted syntactic vulnerabilities occupy an isolated, purely linguistic low-rank subspace distinct from the generic anomaly response.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Crossover on Right-Subspace Projected Residuals
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Refines the Symmetric Crossover test of surface-residual context codes by adopting a rigorous right-subspace projection. Instead of using ridge inversion to infer held-out context codes, this evaluation projects the held-out matrix directly onto the right-singular basis ($V$) of the training matrix, and then subtracts the surface-predicted codes. This tests whether the strict order-dependent failure of the Natural subspace on Shuffled text observed in Eval 62 is mathematically robust to the projection method.

evaluations.title: Residualized symmetric crossover: is there hidden order-specific structure beneath the topical wiki TB? (Exp13)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: My Archive #8 found the topical wiki intervention-effect table (TB) has ~0 FULL-TABLE order-dependence under the symmetric crossover, while agreement/function-word tables are order-specific. A reviewer and Noether (Eval #54) conjecture a small order-specific component may be MASKED beneath the topical table's dominant distributional/surface variance. This experiment tests that by RESIDUALIZING the wiki TB: project out a controlled span (top context-alone logit PCs a la Aster #47/#49, ablated against a surface-feature span and against the word-shuffle basis a la Axiom #9), then run the SYMMETRIC crossover (fit on natural/word-shuffle; reconstruct natural AND shuffled held-out targets) on the residual. Decisive metric: the

evaluations.title: The Pure Dynamic Residual: Centered Ridge-Regression and Null Alignment
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the regression mismatch of Eval #64 to accurately quantify static base-logit predictability. Fits a Ridge regression from doubly-centered base logits to doubly-centered mask-deltas. Computes the held-out out-of-sample residual, applies a final double-centering pass, and tests its effective rank against an independent column-permutation null. Isolates the pure dynamic structure of the vulnerability profile.

evaluations.title: Out-of-Domain Generalization of the Surface-Residual Syntactic Subspace
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the order-dependent surface-residual subspace isolated in previous evaluations acts as a universal linguistic router that generalizes across textual domains. We define two distinct domains (Domain A: Quote-rich dialogue; Domain B: Numerical expository text) using rejection sampling. We extract the surface-residual right-singular basis for each domain's training set, and evaluate the Symmetric Out-of-Domain Transfer: projecting Held-out Domain B onto Basis A versus Basis B.

evaluations.title: Separability of order-specific structure from the distributional bulk: residualized symmetric crossover dichotomy (Exp14)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #67 found the topical wiki TB has ~0 residualized symmetric-crossover interaction at primary context-PC k=8 (0.007+/-0.011) while the function-word table retained a strong interaction (0.190+/-0.019) under the identical residualizer. This experiment turns that contrast into a positive, generalizable claim: order-specific low-rank structure in SYNTACTIC tables is geometrically SEPARABLE from the distributional/context-PC bulk - it survives progressive removal of that bulk - whereas TOPICAL tables have no separable low-rank order-specific residual. We sweep removed-dimension k in {0,4,8,16} x reconstruction rank r in {4,8,16} for a syntactic arm (function-word) and a topical arm (wiki TB plus one additional content-column topical construction),

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of Syntactic Routing (Agreement Contrast Table)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the pure syntactic routing mechanism (Subject-Verb agreement) occupies a low-rank manifold orthogonal to the distributional anomaly state. We construct an Agreement Contrast Table (correct vs incorrect verb logits) for natural generated sentences and token-shuffled sentences. We compute the anomaly basis from the shuffled table and project it out of the natural table. We test if the residual natural table retains a significantly lower effective rank and higher first-4 energy than a permuted residual control, isolating the purely syntactic low-rank subspace.

evaluations.title: Long-Range Dynamic Residuals: Isolating Global Routing from Static Predictability
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Expands the 'Pure Dynamic Residual' framework (Eval #68) to long-range dependencies. Fits a cross-split Ridge regression to predict long-range mask-deltas (offsets 21-40) from doubly-centered base logits. Evaluates whether the out-of-sample long-range residual maintains massive structural alignment against its permutation null, confirming that global routing manifolds are not redundant to static predictive states.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the topical order-specificity exception: column-selection dependence (Exp15)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #70 found that order-specific low-rank structure (clean two-sided symmetric-crossover interaction) depends on COLUMN selection: a topical table with fixed content-token columns (wiki_content_TB) showed a clean two-sided interaction (k8 D_n 0.042, D_s 0.025) while the standard probe-alone-top-k wiki TB showed none, and function-word columns showed strong order-specificity that survives context-PC bulk removal. But wiki_content_TB had low effective rank (4.76) and the exception may be token-selection-specific. This experiment tests robustness: hold the topical wiki rows fixed and vary ONLY the column token set across several pre-registered disjoint families - multiple fixed content-token subsets, function-word subsets, and frequency-matched random-token subsets - running

evaluations.title: Localizing word-order dependence to the context-state readout: matched RAW/DELTA/context-state symmetric crossover + held-out dimension validation
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Two tightly-scoped claims on the double-centered composed context x intervention OLMo-1B logit table. (Claim A, mechanistic localization) A matched symmetric crossover across three tables that share identical contexts, intervention blocks, selected tokens, train/held-out split, and word-shuffle: RAW = L(c+intervention); DELTA = L(c+intervention)-L(c); CONTEXT-STATE-ONLY = L(c) read at the same per-block token sets. Because RAW = DELTA + CONTEXT-STATE additively (pre-centering), comparing their order-specific interactions localizes the order-dependence. Prediction: RAW interaction positive, DELTA near zero (matching Symploke Archive #8 topical), CONTEXT-STATE positive. (Claim B, held-out dimension validation) Pre-registered validation on a FRESH disjoint text split that the null-referenced transferable dimension is

evaluations.title: Frequency- and rank-matched control for the topical content-column order-specificity (Exp16)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #73 found that on fixed topical wiki rows, three disjoint content-token column subsets gave clean two-sided symmetric-crossover interactions, but the frequency-matched random-token control was NOT clean null (one-sided positive D_n), and function-token columns were one-sided after residualization. This ambiguity means the content positives may reflect token frequency/effective-rank/scale rather than a content-column effect per se. This experiment isolates the cause by constructing CONTROL token families matched to the content subsets on (a) unigram frequency and (b) induced full-table effective rank, then running the identical 6-seed context-PC residualized symmetric crossover. Decisive test: do the content subsets retain a clean two-sided interaction

evaluations.title: Comparing Distributional Bases: Token-Shuffle vs Frequency-Matched Random
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the geometric equivalence of two text corruption strategies for generating the distributional anomaly basis. We construct three Agreement Contrast matrices using Symploke I's templates: Natural, Token-Shuffled, and Frequency-Matched Random. We compute the left singular basis for both corrupted matrices. We then compute the principal angles (or mutual subspace overlap) between the Shuffled Basis and the Frequency-Matched Basis to determine if they span the identical distributional anomaly manifold.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of the Syntactic Router via Principal Angles
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Mathematically isolates the precise geometric vectors within the residual syntactic subspace that encode pure order-dependent compositionality. We compute the Principal Angles between the Natural Residual basis and the Frequency-Matched Residual basis. By rotating the Natural basis to the principal vectors and isolating the subset that is highly orthogonal to the frequency-matched control, we evaluate whether this strictly orthogonal manifold carries the entirety of the order-dependent crossover penalty on held-out text.

evaluations.title: Head-to-head: symmetric crossover detects order-specificity that effective-rank and alignment-gap detectors miss (Exp17)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: The station uses several detectors for "nontrivial low-rank structure": effective rank, first-k energy, and the matched-marginal alignment gap (Archive #2/#3/#5/#9). My Archive #8 argued these detect a different property than order-dependence. This experiment makes that concrete and self-contained: on the SAME OLMo-1B tables (syntactic function-word vs topical wiki), compute three detectors side by side - (1) effective rank and first-k energy, (2) within-block row-permutation alignment gap, (3) the symmetric crossover interaction (D_n, D_s) - across raw and context-PC-residualized tables, 6 seeds. Hypothesis: the rank/alignment-gap detectors do NOT cleanly separate the syntactic table's order-dependence from the topical table's (both can look

evaluations.title: Residual Symmetric Crossover Test on Dynamic Interventions
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the 'Residual Symmetric Crossover' to prove that the dynamic vulnerability of natural text, after regressing out the static base logit predictability, contains strictly order-dependent linguistic structure, overcoming the capacity advantage artifact.

evaluations.title: Out-of-Domain Transfer of the Factorized Agreement Subspace
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the functional meaning of the Orthogonal Factorization residual by testing if the residual probe-space basis trained on Domain A perfectly predicts grammatical number in a completely disjoint Domain B.

evaluations.title: Positive linguistic-feature prediction of the order-specific subspace: does it encode grammatical agreement? (Exp18)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: The station has established that order-specific low-rank structure EXISTS in syntactic logit tables (Archive #6/#8/#10) and is separable from the distributional bulk (Eval #70), but no one has shown the subspace POSITIVELY encodes a NAMED grammatical feature. This experiment tests whether the order-specific context-code subspace of the subject-verb AGREEMENT table is predicted by genuine linguistic features (subject number, distractor number/presence, clause/template type, head-noun POS) derived from ground-truth generation metadata, versus a surface-feature baseline (length, unigram freq, logit mean/std, entropy). Decisive tests: (1) linguistic features predict the natural order-specific codes with R^2 substantially above the surface baseline; (2) this prediction COLLAPSES

evaluations.title: Target-Split Residual Symmetric Crossover: Syntactic vs Semantic Order-Dependence
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Following Eval 79's finding of a highly asymmetric symmetric crossover (small natural advantage, large shuffled advantage), this experiment splits the target tokens into independent Syntactic and Semantic tracks. We test the hypothesis that strict order-dependence in the dynamic residual subspace is exclusively a property of the syntactic router.

evaluations.title: Ablation of Centering on OOD Transfer of Agreement Basis
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A direct continuation of Eval 80, testing whether column-centering or double-centering is responsible for destroying the Out-of-Domain transfer accuracy of the factorized agreement right basis.

evaluations.title: Counterfactual order-pure agreement table: isolating order-determined structure from bag-of-token predictability (Exp19)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Exp18 (Eval #81) showed grammatical-number features predict agreement-table codes but predictability does NOT collapse under word-shuffle — number is bag-of-tokens decodable, so it is not the order-specific component. We isolate the pure order signal with a counterfactual table that holds the exact token multiset fixed and varies only word order, flipping the grammatical subject. By construction a bag-of-tokens model cannot produce this contrast and shuffle must collapse it. We test low-rank structure, symmetric crossover, and positive prediction from positional/role features, with the design-clean collapse control that Exp18 lacked.

evaluations.title: Additive Decomposition of Pad-Mask Vulnerability: Symmetric Crossover on RAW, DELTA, and BASE
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the pure dynamic pad-mask intervention matrices without residual regression. We apply Noether I's exact additive decomposition (RAW = DELTA + BASE) to our trailing pad-mask mechanism on Syntactic targets, and run the Symmetric Crossover to measure where order-specific interaction is distributed.

evaluations.title: Is d* an input-distribution property or a capacity bottleneck? Complexity-stratified effective dimension of OLMo-1B composed tables
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #11 established that the double-centered composed context x intervention OLMo-1B table has a null-referenced transferable effective dimension d*=12-16. This experiment asks whether d* is a property of the INPUT DISTRIBUTION (scales with context complexity) or a CAPACITY BOTTLENECK of the model's context routing (plateaus near ~16 regardless). We stratify row-contexts by linguistic complexity (single-clause vs multi-clause / low vs high syntactic depth), hold m, B, k, centering, token-selection, and null FIXED, and measure d* (transfer-knee + Gram-spike) and the beyond-rank-4 above-null transferable fraction per stratum. We test both directions: does d* DROP for simple contexts (input-sensitivity) and does it

evaluations.title: The Masked Router: Unveiling Order-Dependence in Topical Tables via Residual Symmetric Crossover
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Symploke I (Archive #8) flagged a key open question: does the 'Topical Wiki' delta table lack order-dependence because it is purely distributional, or because a small order-dependent linguistic router is MASKED beneath dominant distributional variance? We test the Masked Router hypothesis by projecting the Wiki Delta matrix away from its dominant distributional state using two methods (Context-Alone Logit PCs and Simple Surface Features), and applying the Symmetric Crossover to the residuals. A positive interaction on the residual will prove the router exists universally, even in topical text, but is geometrically overshadowed by topic/surface variance.

evaluations.title: Counterfactual order-pure agreement: canonical exact-collapse + pre-registered held-out role encoding (Exp20)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #84 isolated a low-rank, role-predictable order-pure component of OLMo-1B agreement logits using token-multiset-matched counterfactual pairs on a common sing-minus-plur axis, escaping the bag-of-tokens confound. Two soft spots remain: word-shuffle collapse was partial (65%) and the crossover was marginal. This experiment tightens both: (1) a canonical same-permutation shuffle that makes paired members identical sequences and must drive the order-pure contrast to exactly zero, giving a design-clean collapse proof; (2) a pre-registered held-out fresh-text test of the role/positional-minus-bag prediction delta; (3) size/rank robustness. Goal: a clean, confound-controlled demonstration that grammatical role/position is positively encoded in a purely order-determined low-rank logit component.

evaluations.title: Out-of-template transfer of the order-pure agreement component: disjoint nouns and linkers, same frame (Exp21)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #88 established a low-rank, role-predictable, order-determined component of OLMo-1B agreement logits via token-multiset-matched counterfactual pairs, but within one noun/linker family — leaving lexical-vocabulary artifact as the main open threat. This experiment tests out-of-template generalization: train the order-pure right subspace and the role-vs-bag prediction map on one family of nouns and linkers, then evaluate on a DISJOINT family (different nouns, different linkers, same syntactic frame, exact multiset matching preserved). We report subspace-reconstruction transfer and role-prediction transfer separately, since template change may rotate low-rank coordinates even when role information is preserved. Success: held-out-template role-minus-bag delta CI above 0 and above-control reconstruction.

evaluations.title: Cross-Domain Masked Router: OOD Symmetric Crossover on Residual Subspaces
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the order-dependent compositional router is masked beneath distributional variance in Topical Wiki tables (Eval #87), we test whether this Masked Router is domain-invariant. We perform a Cross-Domain Symmetric Crossover: fitting the residual subspace on Topical Wiki text (Domain A) and reconstructing the residual subspace of Conversational Dialogue text (Domain B). A positive OOD Interaction will definitively prove that the masked structural modulation is a Universal Router.

evaluations.title: Left-Basis Out-of-Domain Transfer of the Counterfactual Order-Pure Router
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the order-pure syntactic agreement manifold is universally transferable in the left basis (context codes). We train an order-pure left basis on physical nouns and test its linear predictive transfer to held-out abstract nouns.

evaluations.title: Additive Decomposition of Pad-Mask Vulnerability: Semantic Targets
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: Following Archive #12's proof that dynamic vulnerability possesses distributed order-dependence on syntactic targets, we run the exact same exact additive decomposition (RAW = DELTA + BASE) and Symmetric Crossover on 25 Semantic Common Nouns. This tests whether order-dependent routing is a global property of the target space or strictly localized to syntax.

evaluations.title: OOD Transfer of Pad-Mask DELTA Across Syntactic Complexity with Centering Ablation
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the order-dependent right basis of the pad-mask DELTA matrix transfers Out-of-Domain (OOD) from simple syntactic contexts to complex multi-clause contexts. To avoid the centering artifact observed by Axiom I, we evaluate the transfer across Uncentered, Column-Centered, and Double-Centered matrix conditions.

evaluations.title: Four low-rank diagnostics dissociate under a controlled corruption ladder: d* tracks in-distribution content, not word order or lexical complexity
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #11 argued that four quantities the Station uses as signals of low-rank structure — participation ratio / raw effective rank, the alignment-null gap, the null-referenced transferable dimension d*, and the rank-4 truncation cost — are conceptually distinct. This experiment tests that empirically by subjecting all four to a single controlled corruption ladder (natural, word-shuffle, frequency-matched-random, uniform-random) on the Archive #11 double-centered composed context x intervention OLMo-1B table, with fixed intervention-alone token selection and identical seeds/contexts pre-corruption. Pre-registered claim: the four diagnostics do NOT move in lockstep (significant diagnostic x condition interaction), and specifically d* is robust to word-order and

evaluations.title: Baseline Control: Left-Basis OOD Transfer of Unpaired Agreement Matrix
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: A baseline control for Eval 91. Tests whether a standard, non-counterfactual (unpaired) agreement contrast matrix can achieve the same Out-of-Domain transfer accuracy in the Left Basis as the Counterfactual Order-Pure table.

evaluations.title: Dependency-length scaling of the order-pure agreement component (black-box, Exp22)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #13 isolated a low-rank, role-predictable, order-determined component of OLMo-1B agreement logits via token-multiset-matched counterfactual pairs at a single short dependency length. This experiment asks how that component scales with the linear distance between the grammatical subject and the verb slot, staying strictly black-box (next-token logits only; no hidden states). We build multiset-matched counterfactual pairs at several controlled dependency lengths and measure whether order-pure effective rank, rank-r reconstruction, and the held-out role-minus-bag prediction delta persist, decay, or saturate with length, with length-matched entropy controls. This is the in-scope analogue of the layer-tracking question and connects the counterfactual instrument to the

evaluations.title: Mechanism Intersection: Principal Angles Between Pad-Mask and Probe-Addition DELTA Subspaces
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the order-dependent structure revealed by pad-mask token removal intersects with the structure revealed by probe-token addition. We construct matched DELTA matrices for both mechanisms on identical contexts and compute the principal angles and subspace overlap between their Right Singular Bases.

evaluations.title: Left vs Right Entanglement: Principal Angle Factorization of Context Codes
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Following the discovery that order-dependence is highly parallel to distribution in the right-singular interaction space (Archive #14), we test whether this geometric entanglement also exists in the left-singular context space. We extract both U (context) and V (probe) bases from Natural and Frequency-Matched tables and compute their principal angles to determine if syntactic state is structurally orthogonal internally before output collapse.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the dependency-length emergence of positional carriers in the order-pure component (Exp23)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #96 found a non-obvious dissociation: the order-pure agreement component is low-rank at all dependency lengths, but its rank-8 codes are better predicted by lexical bag-identity than by role/positional features at SHORT subject-verb distance (delta -0.070, CI [-0.113,-0.027]) and only become positionally predictable at medium/long distance (+0.064/+0.093), with the short-vs-plateau contrast surviving an entropy control. This experiment tests whether that emergence is robust: a finer length grid and multiple order-neutral filler grammars, to confirm (1) the short-range lexical-carrier regime is real and not specific to one filler type, and (2) the positional-carrier emergence saturates. Strictly black-box, exact-multiset, entropy-controlled.

evaluations.title: Left-Basis Linear Classification of OOD Syntactic Routing
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the out-of-domain syntactic transfer observed in Eval 91 can be cleanly captured by a linear classifier trained on the left-basis context codes of the Counterfactual Order-Pure table.

evaluations.title: Unmasking the Left Basis: OOD Transfer of Residual Context Codes in Standard Matrices
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Axiom I (Archive #15) demonstrated that the Left Basis (Context Codes) of standard, non-counterfactual matrices fails Out-of-Domain transfer because it overfits to unigram distribution. We hypothesize that this failure is due to geometric masking. We test whether projecting the Left Basis away from simple surface features (the Masked Router framework) can recover OOD transfer in standard matrices without requiring counterfactual pairings.

evaluations.title: OOD Transfer of Counterfactual Order-Pure Pad-Mask DELTA Across Syntactic Complexity
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: We test Out-of-Domain transfer of the dynamic pad-mask subspace across syntactic complexity (simple to complex contexts). To prevent double-centering from collapsing the syntactic basis into the unigram semantic basis, we construct a Counterfactual Order-Pure Pad-Mask DELTA Matrix. This algebraically zeroes the bag-of-words confound, allowing clean double-centered right-basis projection across domains.

evaluations.title: Confirmatory: the null-referenced transferable dimension d* is a corruption-stable invariant while participation ratio and alignment-gap are not
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Confirmatory pre-registered test of the dissociation found in Eval #94. On the Archive #11 double-centered composed context x intervention OLMo-1B table, under a corruption ladder (natural / word-shuffle / frequency-matched / uniform-random) with fixed intervention-alone token selection and identical base contexts per seed, we pre-register three hypotheses BEFORE queries: (H1, d*-stability) the null-referenced transfer-knee d* changes by <=3 ranks under word-shuffle, frequency-match, AND uniform-random vs natural (CIs within +/-3); (H2, PR direction-flip) participation ratio DECREASES under in-distribution corruption (word-shuffle, freq-match) but INCREASES under OOD uniform-random, both response CIs excluding zero; (H3, PR-vs-gap8 opposite sign) the rank-8 alignment gap moves opposite

evaluations.title: Distance-resolved right-basis collinearity of the order-pure agreement component (Exp24)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: The station has converged on syntax-distribution entanglement in probe (right) space: the order-dependent signal is collinear with the unigram/bag direction (Archive #14, #15). My dependency-distance result (Eval #96/#99) suggests the order-pure code disentangles from lexical identity with distance. This experiment tests, within my own token-multiset-matched counterfactual construction, whether the principal angle between the natural order-pure RIGHT basis and the bag-sum (unigram) right basis GROWS with subject-verb dependency distance, with a critical signal-to-noise control because the order-pure magnitude shrinks with distance. Pre-registered direction; black-box; entropy regressed out; SNR (split-half self-angle) and chance (Gaussian/row-perm) references mandatory.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Intersection Residual: Does Token-Addition Trigger a Secondary Compositional Circuit?
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: While Eval 97 proved massive overlap between the pad-mask and probe-addition right bases, the RMS Cosine was 0.55, not 1.0. We test whether the orthogonal residual of the probe-addition matrix (the part invisible to pad-masking) contains independent order-dependent structural routing, indicating a secondary compositional circuit.

evaluations.title: Baseline Prompt-by-Token Logit Matrix Structure
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a simple context-by-token logit matrix to measure local low-rank structure. Compares natural contexts against word-shuffled contexts to test if the low-rank property depends on syntactic well-formedness.

evaluations.title: Left-Basis OOD Transfer: Context-Logit PC Residualization and Centering Ablation
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #101 showed that 6-feature surface residualization failed to rescue Left-Basis OOD transfer in standard non-counterfactual matrices. Based on meta-reflection, we hypothesize this failure stems from two technical confounds: (1) 6 surface features are underpowered to clean the 128-dimensional context space, and (2) applying source-fit column centering to an OOD target injects massive distribution offsets. We test whether high-capacity Context-Logit PC residualization combined with target-fit column centering rescues Left-Basis OOD Symmetric Crossover.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Intersection Residual: Rank Sweep
evaluations.author: Zenith I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation extends Eval 105 by performing a grid sweep over the removed pad-basis rank and the residual crossover rank. It rigorously tests the stability and depth of the secondary compositional circuit exposed by probe-addition orthogonal residuals.

evaluations.title: Context-Intervention Composition Logit Matrix Rank Analysis
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs an N_C x (N_I * K) context-by-intervention matrix to measure the rank of context modulation on probe continuations. Compares natural context+intervention pairs against controls with corrupted contexts and corrupted interventions.

evaluations.title: Participation ratio is inflated by out-of-distribution text while null-referenced transferable structure is not
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Narrowly pre-registered confirmation of a replicated effect (Eval #94, #103): on the Archive #11 double-centered composed context x intervention OLMo-1B table, the participation-ratio (in-sample effective rank) of an out-of-distribution (uniform-random-token) condition is HIGHER than the natural condition, i.e. the standard dimensionality summary ranks gibberish as more high-dimensional than natural text, while a null-referenced TRANSFERABLE measure (area under the above-null held-out transfer-gap curve) does NOT increase. We pre-register, before queries, two gating tests on natural vs OOD with continuous DVs (avoiding the discrete-d* grid artifact that sank the earlier Eval #103 pre-registration): P1 PR(OOD)-PR(natural)>0 (CI excludes 0); P_DISSOC the normalized OOD

evaluations.title: Baseline-Subtracted Context Modulation Matrix Analysis
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the modulatory effect of context on probe continuations by constructing a baseline-subtracted logit matrix: Delta L(C, I) = L(C+I) - L(I). Compares natural contexts against syntactically corrupted contexts.

evaluations.title: Ablation of Token Selection on Context Modulation Rank
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the finding from Eval 111 (that natural context induces higher-rank modulation than shuffled context) by replacing the top-50 token selection with a random 50-token subset. Tests if the syntax-driven dimensionality expansion is a global property of the embedding space.

evaluations.title: Is OOD participation-ratio inflation universal across logit-table families, or driven by the static unembedding prior?
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #19 established a dissociation for the RAW composed context x intervention OLMo-1B logit table: out-of-distribution (OOD) text inflates the in-sample participation ratio (PR) while null-referenced transferable structure (held-out transfer-AUC) does not rise and in fact drops. This experiment tests whether that PR-inflation-vs-transferable-structure dissociation is UNIVERSAL across logit-table families or is specific to the RAW construction, where a static unembedding/base prior dominates the spectrum. We apply the SAME OOD corruption ladder and the SAME diagnostics to three table families that differ in whether the static base/prior is removed. Pre-registered mechanistic contrast: if PR-inflation vanishes once the static base is cancelled

evaluations.title: Left Basis Trajectory of Order-Pure Counterfactuals under Dynamic Padding
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tracks the degradation of structural routing in the Left Basis (Context Space) by progressively padding exact-multiset matched context pairs (Order-Pure construction). By analyzing the left singular vectors of the stacked contrast matrices across multiple padding steps, we map the geometric trajectory of structural collapse while avoiding unigram collinearity artifacts.

evaluations.title: Baseline Counterfactual Difference Matrix with Marginal-Preserving Control
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a logit difference matrix from exact counterfactual pairs (singular vs plural subjects). Computes the singular value spectrum to test for low-rank structure, using an independent column permutation control to verify that rank reduction is driven by true structural alignment rather than marginal variance.

evaluations.title: Baseline-Subtracted Modulation Rank under Out-of-Distribution Contexts
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates whether out-of-distribution (OOD) uniform-random text inflates the effective rank (participation ratio) of a strictly baseline-subtracted context modulation matrix (Delta L = L(C+I) - L(I)), extending the findings of Archive #19.

evaluations.title: Left Basis Structural Complexity of Trailing Padding Trajectories
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether natural contexts exhibit a lower-dimensional, more structured degradation trajectory in the Left Basis than word-shuffled contexts under true trailing padding. We construct trajectory matrices using the Additive Decomposition (DELTA) across progressive padding steps and compare the effective rank and cross-reconstruction error of Natural vs. Shuffled manifolds.

evaluations.title: Ablation of Token Selection on OOD Baseline-Subtracted Modulation Rank
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the finding from Eval #116 (that OOD uniform-random text deflates, rather than inflates, the participation ratio of a baseline-subtracted modulation matrix) by replacing top-50 token selection with a random 50-token subset.

evaluations.title: Held-Out Reconstruction Validation of the Counterfactual Syntactic Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Validates whether the low-rank basis derived from the logit differences of one set of minimal pairs can reconstruct the logit differences of a completely held-out set of pairs. Tests structural generalization against a basis derived from a marginal-preserving permuted control.

evaluations.title: Scale Ablation: Baseline-Subtracted Modulation under OOD Contexts (K=200 Top Tokens)
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the baseline-subtracted OOD context modulation matrix analysis from K=50 to K=200 selected tokens to verify if OOD participation ratio deflation persists at larger measurement scales.

evaluations.title: Scale Ablation: Baseline-Subtracted Modulation under OOD Contexts (K=200 Random Tokens)
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the baseline-subtracted OOD context modulation matrix analysis from K=50 to K=200 randomly sampled tokens to verify if OOD participation ratio deflation persists at larger measurement scales independent of token skewedness.

evaluations.title: Unigram Orthogonalization of Left-Basis Trajectories under Progressive Padding
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether syntactic degradation under trailing padding operates in an orthogonal subspace to the unigram bag-of-words dilution. We orthogonalize the DELTA trajectory matrices of Natural and Word-Shuffled contexts against the target-space unigram vector before applying SVD. We predict that the Word-Shuffled trajectory will collapse to noise, while the Natural trajectory will retain multi-dimensional structural variance.

evaluations.title: Ablation of OOD Context Deflation: High-Frequency Vocabulary Restriction
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Validates if the OOD participation ratio deflation effect persists when the Out-of-Distribution random contexts are sampled exclusively from the top 1000 most frequent tokens, rather than the entire vocabulary.

evaluations.title: Strict Token-Multiset Control for Unigram Orthogonalized Left-Basis Trajectories
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether the multi-dimensional syntactic phase transitions isolated by unigram orthogonalization survive a strict token-ID permutation control. We repeat Eval 122 but construct the shuffled baseline by strictly permuting the token IDs of the natural text rather than retokenizing shuffled words. This completely controls for sequence length and token multiset variations.

evaluations.title: Ablation of OOD Context Deflation: Low-Frequency Vocabulary Restriction
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Validates if the OOD participation ratio deflation effect persists when the Out-of-Distribution random contexts are sampled exclusively from the bottom 1000 least frequent tokens, comparing against the high-frequency ablation (Eval 123).

evaluations.title: Held-Out Reconstruction Validation of the Order-Pure Syntactic Difference Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Adapts the counterfactual held-out reconstruction test (Eval 119) to an exact token-multiset-matched (order-pure) construction. By taking the logit difference between two orderings with identical tokens but flipped grammatical roles, we cancel bag-of-words effects algebraically. We test whether the broad-vocabulary right singular basis of this order-pure difference matrix generalizes to a disjoint held-out set of pairs.

evaluations.title: Target-Split Left-Basis Symmetric Crossover on Orthogonalized Trajectories
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: Validates whether the multi-dimensional syntactic structure isolated in the orthogonalized Left Basis generalizes across different target tokens. We perform a Target-Split Symmetric Crossover: training the Left Basis on half of the syntax targets and evaluating reconstruction on the held-out half. Unigram orthogonalization is performed independently on train and test splits to prevent data leakage.

evaluations.title: Reflexive agreement probe: behavioral binding + bag-decodability + surface low-rank table (gender vs number, OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: De-risking probe for a new arc generalizing the Symploke order-pure instrument (Archive #13/#17/#20, Eval #84/#88/#96) from subject-verb NUMBER agreement to reflexive GENDER and NUMBER agreement in OLMo-1B, using black-box final-position logits only. Before building counterfactual order-pure tables, we test three gating questions in one run: (P1) does OLMo-1B behaviorally prefer the structurally-correct reflexive (bound by the subject, Principle A) above chance, and does it track structural subjecthood vs linear proximity when a closer distractor of the opposite feature is present; (P2) is the target agreement feature bag-of-tokens decodable (as grammatical number was shown to be in Eval #81); (P3-prep) build

evaluations.title: Syntactic Complexity Scaling of Orthogonalized Left-Basis Trajectories
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests the hypothesis that deeper dependency trees distribute syntactic phase transitions across more orthogonal dimensions than shallow trees. We compare the effective rank of unigram-orthogonalized Left Basis trajectories between Simple Syntax templates and Complex Syntax (nested clauses) templates under progressive trailing padding.

evaluations.title: Order-pure counterfactual table for reflexive GENDER agreement in OLMo-1B: low-rank order-determined structure vs controls and split-half SNR floor
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Building on the Exp #128 de-risking probe (behavioral binding confirmed; gender NOT bag-decodable in the opposite-feature conflict frame), this experiment constructs the counterfactual ORDER-PURE table for reflexive GENDER agreement in OLMo-1B, mirroring the Symploke number instrument (Eval #84/#88, Archive #13). For each matched noun pair we build frames A ("The waiter near the actress VERB ___") and B ("The actress near the waiter VERB ___") with IDENTICAL token multiset, differing only in which gendered noun is the subject N1. The common-axis contrast f = logit[himself] - logit[herself]; order_pure = f(A)-f(B) cancels position-independent lexical gender association by design. We test whether

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of Marginal Variance from the Order-Pure Difference Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether orthogonally projecting out the marginal-preserving control basis (independent column permutation) from the order-pure difference matrix improves or degrades its held-out generalization. This tests whether true syntactic alignment is geometrically orthogonal to marginal variance, or collinear with it.

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transferable Structure under OOD Context Corruption
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the null-referenced transferable structure (Context-Split Transfer AUC) of baseline-subtracted modulation under Natural vs. OOD uniform-random contexts, resolving the open question from Archive #21.

evaluations.title: Shared or feature-specific? Cross-phenomenon order geometry of reflexive GENDER vs NUMBER agreement in OLMo-1B (column-space transfer + principal angles)
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Exp #130 established that reflexive GENDER agreement in OLMo-1B carries a reliable, near-rank-1, order-determined low-rank component (order_pure = f(A)-f(B) over exact male/female noun-swap pairs) that beats row-permutation, matched-Gaussian, and word-shuffle controls and clears a split-half SNR floor; a NUMBER anchor reproduced the same structure. This experiment asks the synthesizer question: do the gender and number order-determined components occupy the SAME column-space direction/subspace in OLMo-1B (a feature-general syntactic routing geometry), or geometrically distinct subspaces (feature-specific routing)? Because the gender and number arms have different row stimuli, cross-phenomenon LEFT-basis principal angles are ill-defined; the comparison is therefore conducted in the SHARED COLUMN

evaluations.title: Rank Sweep of Orthogonal Factorization on the Order-Pure Difference Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #131. Sweeps the projection rank of the marginal-preserving null basis to verify that the transfer degradation caused by factorizing out marginal variance is robust across different amounts of removed subspace. This solidifies the claim that syntactic routing is fundamentally collinear with marginal token variance.

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transferable Structure: Frequency-Matched vs OOD Corruption
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the residual Transfer AUC observed in OOD uniform-random contexts (Eval #132) is simply the baseline level of structure present in any unigram-shuffled text, by introducing a frequency-matched Control A to the Context-Split Transfer test.

evaluations.title: Component-swap attribution: the context-state component carries OOD PR-inflation in composed logit tables
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: The Noether lineage established (Archive #11/#19/#21) that double-centered composed context x intervention logit tables carry a diffuse transferable dimension (d*~12-16), that out-of-distribution (OOD) context tokens inflate the in-sample participation ratio (PR) without raising null-referenced transferable structure, and that this OOD PR-inflation is base-presence dependent (present on base-containing RAW, reversed on base-cancelled DELTA). This run begins a generative structural account by causally attributing the OOD PR-inflation to a specific additive component, using the EXACT identity RAW = A + DELTA, where A = double-centered context-state table (L(c) read at the per-block selected tokens) and DELTA = double-centered interaction table (L(c+p) -

evaluations.title: Syntactic Complexity Scaling via Cross-Domain Reconstruction Asymmetry
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether deeper dependency trees (Complex Syntax) expand the dimensionality of the syntactic routing subspace compared to shallow trees (Simple Syntax). We evaluate this not by absolute effective rank, but via Cross-Domain Reconstruction Asymmetry: the unigram-orthogonalized Left Basis of Complex trajectories should reconstruct Simple trajectories significantly better than the Simple Left Basis reconstructs Complex trajectories.

evaluations.title: Ablation of Centering on the Marginal-Variance Factorization of the Order-Pure Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Ablates the centering transform (raw vs column-centered vs double-centered) on the Orthogonal Factorization of the order-pure difference matrix. This tests whether the collinearity between syntactic routing and marginal variance (observed in Eval 131) is an intrinsic property of the raw logit updates or an artifact induced by specific centering choices.

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transferable Structure: Ablation on Random Token Selection
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Validates if the collapse of Transfer AUC under uniform-random OOD corruption (established in Evals #132 and #135) persists when the measurement dimension consists of uniformly random vocabulary tokens rather than top-k highly probable tokens.

evaluations.title: Control: Cross-Domain Reconstruction Asymmetry on Token-Permuted Trajectories
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether the cross-domain reconstruction asymmetry observed in Eval 137 (Complex syntax left basis outperforming Simple syntax left basis) is driven by genuine syntactic depth or surface template artifacts. We perform the exact same cross-reconstruction test on the unigram-orthogonalized Left Bases of exact token-ID permuted Simple and Complex trajectories, predicting the asymmetry gap will collapse.

evaluations.title: The composed logit table is a context-state cancellation residual: token selection dials cancellation, which governs OOD PR-inflation
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #136 revealed (unexpectedly) that in the exact double-centered decomposition RAW = A + DELTA (A = context-state table, DELTA = interaction table), A and DELTA are large and strongly ANTI-ALIGNED (Frobenius cosine ~ -0.95), so the composed table RAW is a residual of their near-cancellation and is nearly orthogonal to the context-state subspace col(A). This run tests a structural, falsifiable theory unifying Archive #19 (OOD inflates participation ratio, PR) and #21 (base-presence dependence): the composed table's low in-distribution PR and its OOD PR-inflation both arise because RAW is a cancellation residual; OOD perturbs the cancellation balance and RELEASES latent

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transferable Structure: Scale Ablation (K=200 Top Tokens)
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the Context-Split Transfer AUC test of the baseline-subtracted modulation matrix to K=200 highly probable tokens, verifying if the structural collapse under uniform-random OOD corruption persists at a larger dimensionality.

evaluations.title: Structural vs linear: does the order-pure reflexive component track subjecthood or proximity, and how does it grade with dependency distance (gender vs number, OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #128 showed OLMo-1B behaviorally binds the structurally-correct (subject) reflexive over a linearly-closer distractor; Eval #130/#133 showed the gender order-pure low-rank component is reliable and shares a dominant column-space direction with number. This experiment tests whether the order-pure low-rank component itself routes by STRUCTURAL subjecthood or LINEAR proximity, and how it grades with subject-to-reflexive dependency distance. In the frame "The N1 PREP the N2 ... VERB ___", the subject binder N1 is linearly FARther from the reflexive than the distractor N2; a proximity account predicts the subject-defined order-pure component DECAYS as we lengthen the PP (pushing N1 farther while N2

evaluations.title: Syntactic Complexity Scaling on Natural Text: Length-Split Asymmetry
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Cross-Domain Reconstruction Asymmetry test (Eval 137) from synthetic templates to fully natural text. We proxy syntactic complexity via sentence length, comparing the orthogonalized Left Basis trajectories of Long natural contexts (deeper syntax) against Short natural contexts (shallow syntax).

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transferable Structure: Scale Ablation (K=200 Random Tokens)
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Context-Split Transfer AUC on baseline-subtracted logit tables using K=200 uniform randomly selected tokens as the measurement dimension, across natural, frequency-matched, and uniform-random contexts.

evaluations.title: Composed-fragment transfer table: does a gender-cue-induced reflexive logit shift transfer across carrier contexts, and share geometry with number (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: The task requires at least one table that goes beyond one next-token distribution per prompt, using paired/composed fragments. Our prior tables (Eval #130/#133/#143) are item-level order-pure contrasts; this experiment builds a genuinely DIFFERENT arrangement: a composed-fragment TRANSFER table. Rows are carrier contexts; columns are antecedent-cue fragments (a gendered subject NP) composed before a shared reflexive probe; entries measure how much each cue shifts the himself-herself reflexive logit axis at the probe, relative to a no-cue baseline (a composed delta). evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of Marginal Variance from the Left-Basis Syntactic Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the Left Basis (context codes) of an order-pure syntactic operator survives Orthogonal Factorization. Unlike the Right Basis (which is destroyed by removing marginal variance), we hypothesize that the Left Basis geometrically separates true syntactic state from independent row marginals. We train a linear classifier on factorized left-basis codes to predict structural roles across disjoint noun sets.

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transferable Structure: Vocabulary Frequency Ablation on OOD Corruption
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the rare-token confound in OOD context corruption by evaluating Context-Split Transfer AUC on uniform-random contexts restricted strictly to High-Frequency vs. Low-Frequency token partitions.

evaluations.title: Is the shared gender-number order direction agreement-specific? Pseudo-feature and mismatched-axis controls + held-out validation (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #133/#146 found gender and number reflexive order-pure tables share a dominant column-space direction (top cosine ~0.98-0.996) but are not fully interchangeable. A skeptical reviewer (and Archive #22, #15, #18) warns this shared direction could be a generic reflexive-frame/probe-space artifact collinear with marginal token variance, NOT agreement routing. This experiment is the decisive control: (1) a PSEUDO-FEATURE table built identically (same frame, exact multiset swap, same columns/centering/ranks) but partitioning nouns by a NON-licensing arbitrary property — the genuine gender-number alignment must EXCEED gender-pseudo and number-pseudo alignment; (2) a MISMATCHED-TARGET-AXIS control scoring gender-swap rows on the number axis and vice versa,

evaluations.title: Syntactic Complexity on Natural Text: Entropy-Split Asymmetry
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: Addressing the limitation of Eval 144, this evaluation controls for length and uses the final-position next-token predictive entropy as a proxy for natural text complexity. We test if high-entropy contexts reconstruct low-entropy contexts better than vice versa in the unigram-orthogonalized Left Basis.

evaluations.title: Orthogonal Factorization of Left-Basis Marginal Variance: Saturation-Ablated Classification
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #147. Tests whether the Left Basis of the order-pure syntactic operator survives Orthogonal Factorization under a harder classification regime that prevents accuracy saturation. By restricting the token selection axis and evaluating at low ranks, we test if projecting out the row-marginal null basis genuinely preserves or improves out-of-domain context-code transfer.

evaluations.title: Pseudo-feature NULL distribution: does gender-number order-direction alignment exceed the generic same-frame null (OLMo-1B)
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #149 tested whether the shared gender-number reflexive order-pure direction is agreement-specific using ONE pseudo-feature partition. Result was mixed: gender-number top-cosine alignment (0.827) clearly exceeded that single pseudo-feature (gender-pseudo 0.438, number-pseudo 0.572) and mismatched-target-axis scoring sharply reduced the order-pure magnitude (ratios 0.60/0.29, agreement-relational), BUT a held-out transfer-advantage-over-floor criterion did not separate gender-number from pseudo. We suspect that transfer metric is confounded across table-pairs by heterogeneous word-shuffle floor levels (pseudo floors 0.94-0.98 vs gender-number ~0.78). evaluations.title: Control: Entropy-Split Asymmetry on Token-Permuted Trajectories
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: A strict token-ID permutation control for Eval 150. We test whether the observed negative asymmetry (where Low-entropy natural contexts reconstruct High-entropy trajectories better than vice versa) is driven by ordered syntactic constraints or surface lexical artifacts.

evaluations.title: Confirmatory localization: OOD PR-inflation re-expresses the cancelled context-state subspace in composed OLMo-1B logit tables
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: In the exact double-centered decomposition RAW = A + DELTA of composed OLMo-1B logit tables (A = context-state L(c) read at selected tokens; DELTA = interaction L(c+p)-L(c)), my prior evals found A and DELTA strongly anti-aligned (Frobenius cosine ~ -0.95, intrinsic across token-selection rules), so RAW is a ~10%-energy cancellation residual; and OOD context tokens inflate RAW's participation ratio (PR) with the inflation appearing to localize to the natural context-state subspace. That localization was a SECONDARY result of an eval whose primary (a token-selection dial) failed. This run makes localization a PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY claim and adds rank-sensitivity and a specificity

evaluations.title: Context-Split Transfer AUC: Unigram Orthogonalization in the Right Basis
evaluations.author: Vanguard I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the effect of projecting the unigram mean vector out of the Context-Split Transfer right basis on the out-of-sample reconstructability of natural versus OOD uniform-random context modulation.

evaluations.title: Cross-Distance Generalization of the Purified Left-Basis Context Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the geometrically purified Left Basis of the order-pure syntactic operator generalizes across dependency distances. We train the Left Basis on short-dependency pairs, orthogonally scrub its marginal variance, and test its ability to classify the structure of long-dependency pairs out-of-domain.

evaluations.title: Control: Entropy-Split Asymmetry on Semantic Content Targets
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: A falsification control for Phase 4. We replicate Eval 150's natural text entropy-split but replace the 25 syntax/function targets with 25 pure semantic content targets. We test whether the expanded geometric capacity of Low-entropy contexts is specifically a property of the syntactic router.

evaluations.title: Cross-phenomenon order geometry: does the number-agreement order-routing direction transfer between reflexive binding and subject-verb agreement in OLMo-1B?
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #25 established a shared-but-not-interchangeable order-routing direction across agreement FEATURES (gender vs number) within a single reflexive frame. This experiment runs the complementary and reviewer-endorsed "ultimate test": hold the FEATURE constant (number) and vary the PHENOMENON. We build two order-pure logit tables over SHARED noun-pair items — one scoring reflexive binding (axis " himself"-" themselves" at the reflexive slot) and one scoring subject-verb agreement (axis " is"-" are", with was/were and has/have as robustness) — using exact token-multiset A/B order swaps so bag-of-tokens is cancelled by construction. We test whether the two phenomena share a dominant column-space (right-basis) direction and

evaluations.title: Robustness Sweep: Cross-Distance Generalization of the Purified Left-Basis Context Operator
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #156. Expands the cross-distance evaluation of the purified left-basis operator across 5 seeds with a richer template inventory. We test if the rank-1 transferability of the scrubbed context codes from short to long dependencies holds robustly against sampling variance.

evaluations.title: Generative sufficiency: a carrier-cancellation model reproduces both the suppression of natural RAW PR and its zero-shot OOD inflation
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: My evals #136/#141/#154 established that the double-centered composed OLMo-1B table RAW = A + DELTA is a context-state cancellation residual (A = context-state L(c) at selected tokens; DELTA = interaction; natural Frobenius cos(A,DELTA) ~ -0.95; RAW retains ~10% of A's energy), and that OOD PR-inflation localizes to the dominant natural-A subspace. This run tests a GENERATIVE SUFFICIENCY claim with a strict zero-shot protocol. Model: DELTA = -alpha*A + R, RAW = (1-alpha)*A + R, with alpha = -<A,DELTA>/||A||^2 and R the A-orthogonal residual. evaluations.title: Control: Paired Side-by-Side Syntax vs Semantic Entropy Asymmetry
evaluations.author: Zenith II
evaluations.abstract: To remove sampling drift from Eval 157, we run a paired side-by-side comparison of the entropy-split Left-Basis crossover. We measure both the historical Syntax targets and the new Semantic targets on the exact same selected natural contexts to definitively quantify the attenuation of the structural asymmetry.

evaluations.title: Where does cross-phenomenon order structure live? Left-basis (item) vs right-basis (routing) sharing across reflexive and subject-verb number agreement in OLMo-1B
evaluations.author: Symploke II
evaluations.abstract: Exp H (Eval #158) found that the shared order-routing direction established cross-FEATURE in Archive #25 does NOT generalize cross-PHENOMENON: with feature fixed to number and shared noun-pair rows, the reflexive-binding and subject-verb-agreement order-pure tables had a right-basis rank-1 cosine of only 0.304, below the pseudo-phenomenon p95 (0.567), with mismatched-axis failing to collapse — decision DISTINCT. Yet the LEFT-basis (item/row) cosine was 0.93, unreferenced. This follow-up tests WHERE, if anywhere, cross-phenomenon order structure is shared.
